outline: This course concerns making financial decisions in an uncertain world. Increasingly, financial decision-makers are depending on optimization techniques to guide them in their decisions. We will survey the use of such methods in financial decision-making processes. The optimization techniques to be covered will include linear and nonlinear programming, integer programming, dynamic programming, and nonlinear programming. As a supporting theme, the course will also emphasize effective modeling, the use of modeling languages, such as R for solving financial optimization problems. Also, financial topics to be covered will include also blockchain, cryptocurrency, and portfolio optimization. Blockchain technology enables the execution of collaborative business processes involving untrusted parties without requiring a central authority. A cryptocurrency is a digital or virtual currency designed to work as a medium of exchange. In a decentralized system like cryptocurrency, each and every member needs to carry out this activity. This is done by means of the blockchain. In this course, we learn basic concepts of cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology. Then, we will discuss promising financial optimization issues such as cryptocurrency portfolio diversification.

Week 1 Introduction to financial optimization
Week 2 Linear programming – Simplex method
Week 3 Linear programming – Post-optimal analysis
Week 4 Integer programming
Week 5 Dynamic programming
Week 6 Quadratic programming
Week 7 Stochastic programming
Week 8 Project presentation
Week 9 Midterm Exam (In-Class, 1 Cheat Sheet, Calculator)
Week 10 Nonlinear programming
Week 11 Decision making theory
Week 12 Game theory
Week 13 Heuristic algorithms
Week 14 Artificial neural network (ANN)
Week 15 Introduction to blockchain and cryptocurrency
Week 16 Application of optimization methods to cryptocurrency portfolio diversification
Week 17 Project presentation
Week 18 Final Exam (In-Class, 1 Cheat sheet, Calculator)
Not covers all parts of the course, but covers only what has been discussed after the second midterm.
